Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

Income statement and cash flow lines printed as a dash in the filings (gain on sale of business, loss on sale of property, loss on extinguishment of debt and the matching cash flow lines) are shown as not supplied rather than zero, as the method requires. Severity Low; the totals of the same statements foot without them. The action that would close it is the issuer's confirmation that a dash means nil.

The quarterly reports print no schedule of debt maturities, so the maturity ladder at 2026-09-30 is derived from the annual report's schedule and the stated instalment rate. Severity Medium; it restricts the split of the amount due after 2030 between the last two years. The next annual report would close it.

The unused capacity under the U.S. and Canadian securitization facilities is not stated, so liquidity counts only cash and the revolving facilities. Severity Medium; it understates accessible funding for new loans. The issuer's facility utilisation figures would close it.

The legal rank of the securitization obligations and of the European lines of credit relative to the credit agreement debt is not stated, so both are left out of the debt stack. Severity Medium; the securitization is therefore shown only in the consolidated ratios. The executed agreements would close it.

The covenant ratio of 0.9 reported at 2026-09-30 cannot be reproduced from the statements because its debt, cash and EBITDA definitions are not itemised, and the amendment dated 2026-06-30 is not described. Severity High; it blocks any covenant headroom statement. The credit agreement and the compliance certificate would close it.

Cash interest paid is not split between the securitization borrowings and the corporate debt, so interest cover mixes the two perimeters. Severity Medium; corporate-only cover cannot be stated. A split of cash interest in the next annual report would close it.

Twelve-month figures for 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30 use the issuer's quarterly reconciliations, which have no auditor review. Severity Low; the 2026-09-30 figures match the issuer's own twelve-month table. No further action is needed.

The balance sheet at 2025-09-30 is not supplied, so no leverage point exists for a year earlier than 2026-09-30 other than the year-end figures. Severity Low; the trend is shown at the year-ends and three 2026 quarter-ends.

The assumption that the October 2026 repurchases were paid in cash is Analyst Judgement because the note states the amount but not the funding. Severity Low; the pro forma net debt would be unchanged if funded from cash. The next quarterly report would confirm it.

(opln), as of 2026-11-05, credit_snapshot pathway: the financial foundation for the group, built from the seven supplied filings and earnings slides, with leverage, cover, liquidity and the debt schedule stated on the corporate perimeter and the finance subsidiary's securitization funding shown beside it.

## Findings
### Bottom line

OPENLANE's corporate borrowing is modest at 1.18x total debt to twelve-month EBITDA at 2026-09-30, but the finance subsidiary's USD 2,064.1 million of securitization funding sits outside that figure and is the larger claim on the group's receivables.

Net debt is USD 289.3 million, or 0.64x, after cash rose to USD 244.9 million. On adjusted EBITDA, which deducts securitization interest, total debt is 1.40x. Repurchases of USD 11.1 million in October 2026 would lift net debt to USD 300.4 million, or 0.67x.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C1.5; calculation C4.1; calculation C4.2; calculation C4.3; calculation C6.1; calculation C6.2
### Key findings

Net leverage has fallen from 0.96x at year-end 2025 to 0.64x because twelve-month EBITDA grew to USD 451.5 million and cash rose, while total debt stayed near USD 534.2 million after the 2025 term loan that funded the preferred share repurchase.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59; calculation C1.5; calculation C2.3; calculation C4.2; calculation C4.7

The corporate perimeter leaves out funding that matches the finance subsidiary's receivables: obligations collateralized by finance receivables were USD 2,064.1 million against finance receivables of USD 2,763.8 million, and including them lifts total debt to EBITDA to 5.75x. The securitization lenders look to those receivables through a bankruptcy-remote subsidiary, so they have first recourse to that asset pool ahead of the term loan lenders.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; calculation C3.2; calculation C3.3

The choice of EBITDA measure matters. Reported EBITDA of USD 451.5 million adds back finance interest expense, while adjusted EBITDA of USD 382.7 million deducts USD 95.9 million of securitization interest, so total leverage is 1.18x on the first and 1.40x on the second. Adjusted EBITDA is the better guide to cash that can service the term loan.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59; calculation C4.1; calculation C4.3

Interest cover is 3.42x on reported EBITDA and 2.90x on adjusted EBITDA. The cash interest of USD 132.1 million includes the securitization funding cost, which was USD 106.0 million of finance interest expense over twelve months against USD 37.3 million of corporate interest expense net of interest income, so the cover blends two perimeters and does not isolate the term loan's interest burden.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C4.5; calculation C4.6

Liquidity is USD 650.2 million, being cash of USD 244.9 million and USD 405.3 million of undrawn revolving capacity net of letters of credit. The revolving facilities mature in 2028 and the term loan in 2032, with scheduled amortization of USD 5.5 million a year, so there is no corporate maturity pressure for several years.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C5.5

Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 309.5 million was helped by USD 155.8 million of higher accounts payable and accrued expenses, and accounts payable include sale proceeds owed to consignors. That float reverses when volumes fall, so operating cash flow overstates the cash the business keeps through a downturn.

Shareholder distributions are the main discretionary use of cash: USD 91.5 million of repurchases in nine months, followed by a board decision in October 2026 to enlarge the authorization. Term loan lenders are exposed to a recurring call on cash that the documents do not limit beyond the credit agreement's general dividend and investment covenants.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a benign reading is that the securitization carries most of the group's gearing: consolidated total debt to adjusted EBITDA is 6.79x, and delinquent receivables doubled to 0.6% of receivables managed from 0.3% a year earlier. If delinquency keeps rising, the cash reserve the securitization requires and a tightening of its covenants would draw on the cash that supports the term loan.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation C3.4

The view of low corporate leverage would hold if delinquency stays near 0.6% and provision stays at about 1.1% of average receivables, as in the latest quarter. It would change if reported senior secured net leverage, currently 0.9x against a limit of 3.5x, moved sharply, or if the securitization facilities, now extended to January 2030, were not renewed.
### Limitations
The quarterly reports print no schedule of debt maturities, so the ladder at 2026-09-30 is built from the annual report's schedule less the instalments paid in 2026.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_opln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C7.2
The covenant ratio of 0.9x is the issuer's own figure and its inputs are not itemised, so it cannot be reproduced from the statements and no covenant headroom is worked.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54
Twelve-month figures for the first and second quarters of 2026 are assembled from the issuer's quarterly reconciliations and carry no auditor review.
Basis: EX-99.3_2026-05-05_q12026openlaneearningssl.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; EX-99.3_2026-11-04_q32026openlaneearningssl.htm.jsonl, page 6
The unused capacity under the securitization facilities is not stated, so liquidity counts only cash and the revolving facilities.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56

## Gaps

Income statement and cash flow lines printed as a dash in the filings (gain on sale of business, loss on sale of property, loss on extinguishment of debt and the matching cash flow lines) are shown as not supplied rather than zero, as the method requires. Severity Low; the totals of the same statements foot without them. The action that would close it is the issuer's confirmation that a dash means nil.

The quarterly reports print no schedule of debt maturities, so the maturity ladder at 2026-09-30 is derived from the annual report's schedule and the stated instalment rate. Severity Medium; it restricts the split of the amount due after 2030 between the last two years. The next annual report would close it.

The unused capacity under the U.S. and Canadian securitization facilities is not stated, so liquidity counts only cash and the revolving facilities. Severity Medium; it understates accessible funding for new loans. The issuer's facility utilisation figures would close it.

The legal rank of the securitization obligations and of the European lines of credit relative to the credit agreement debt is not stated, so both are left out of the debt stack. Severity Medium; the securitization is therefore shown only in the consolidated ratios. The executed agreements would close it.

The covenant ratio of 0.9 reported at 2026-09-30 cannot be reproduced from the statements because its debt, cash and EBITDA definitions are not itemised, and the amendment dated 2026-06-30 is not described. Severity High; it blocks any covenant headroom statement. The credit agreement and the compliance certificate would close it.

Cash interest paid is not split between the securitization borrowings and the corporate debt, so interest cover mixes the two perimeters. Severity Medium; corporate-only cover cannot be stated. A split of cash interest in the next annual report would close it.

Twelve-month figures for 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30 use the issuer's quarterly reconciliations, which have no auditor review. Severity Low; the 2026-09-30 figures match the issuer's own twelve-month table. No further action is needed.

The balance sheet at 2025-09-30 is not supplied, so no leverage point exists for a year earlier than 2026-09-30 other than the year-end figures. Severity Low; the trend is shown at the year-ends and three 2026 quarter-ends.

The assumption that the October 2026 repurchases were paid in cash is Analyst Judgement because the note states the amount but not the funding. Severity Low; the pro forma net debt would be unchanged if funded from cash. The next quarterly report would confirm it.

## Findings
### Bottom line

OPENLANE is a scaled digital wholesale vehicle marketplace with a captive floorplan lender, and the sponsor-linked preferred that once ranked ahead of common has converted, which lowers governance risk for term loan lenders but leaves buybacks as the main call on cash.

Marketplace earns 78% of revenue and the finance arm 22%, so credit quality rests on wholesale volumes, which rose 24% in the first nine months of 2026. In October 2025 the company used USD 550.0 million of new secured term loans to buy back preferred stock for USD 559.3 million, a debt-funded take-out of the sponsors that shows willingness to add senior debt for shareholders.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_opln-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation C1.1
### Key findings

The business is two linked franchises: a marketplace that earns fees on volume, and a floorplan lender that depends on the same independent dealers. The marketplace generated 78% of 2025 revenue, and its vehicles sold rose 24% in the first nine months of 2026, with commercial vehicles up 37% on a new private label customer and more off-lease supply.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_opln-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; calculation C1.1; calculation C2.1

Customer concentration is moderate but not fully disclosed. No single customer exceeded 10% of revenue in any year shown, yet commercial volume growth in the third quarter of 2026 was 46% and only 17% without the latest commercial customer, so a few seller programs drive the volume gains.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_opln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 138; EX-99.3_2026-11-04_q32026openlaneearningssl.htm.jsonl, page 4

The sponsor overhang has largely cleared. Preferred cash dividends fell from USD 38.6 million in 2025 to USD 5.3 million in the first nine months of 2026, and all remaining preferred stock converted into common stock in May 2026, which removes a claim that ranked ahead of common stockholders and the cash dividend that came with it.

The October 2025 take-out was funded with debt. Preferred stock repurchased for USD 559.3 million was paid for mainly with USD 550.0 million of incremental secured term loans, so senior claims on the group rose to buy out junior capital. That is the clearest evidence of how the board treats creditors when a holder wants liquidity, and it is the reason governance risk is rated Medium rather than Low.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_opln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C3.1

Capital returns now come from cash flow rather than new debt, but they are large. The company repurchased USD 91.5 million of shares in nine months, including about USD 25 million bought from an underwriter in an August 2026 secondary sale by an Apax affiliate, and in October 2026 the board added USD 150 million to the authorization.

The finance arm is the main source of asset risk. It lends short term to roughly fifteen thousand independent dealers, delinquent receivables rose to 0.6% of receivables managed from 0.3% a year earlier, and securitization lenders fund most of the loan book, so stress at independent dealers would reach group cash flow through lower fees and a larger credit loss provision.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest argument for rating governance risk above Medium is that the 2025 take-out added USD 550.0 million of secured debt to repay holders whose preferred stock had a 7% cumulative dividend, and the company has since bought shares in an Apax affiliate's secondary sale. If the board repeats a debt-funded return, or if the amendment dated 2026-06-30 loosened restricted payment limits, the risk rating would need to be reconsidered upward.

The argument for Low risk is that the preferred holders have converted, an Apax affiliate is selling, buybacks are funded from operating cash flow of USD 309.5 million over nine months, and no new debt-funded distribution has occurred since October 2025. It would win if the remaining sponsor stake falls to a minority and the next annual report shows buybacks below free cash flow.
### Limitations
The proxy statement is not supplied, so board composition, independence and committee roles are not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_opln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 2
The remaining holdings of the Apax and Periphas affiliates after the conversion and the August 2026 secondary sale are not stated, so current sponsor influence cannot be measured.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 66
The terms of the amendment dated 2026-06-30 are not described, so any change to restricted payment capacity is unknown.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_opln-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 65
Customer-level revenue is not disclosed beyond the statement that no customer exceeded a tenth of revenue, so concentration among seller programs cannot be sized.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_opln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 138

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The October 2025 Second Amendment to the Credit Agreement added USD 550.0 million of incremental term loans due 2032-10-08, priced at Adjusted Term SOFR plus 2.50% and amortizing at 0.25% of the original principal each quarter from 2026-03-31. The proceeds financed the repurchase of 334,028 shares of Series A Preferred Stock from affiliates of Apax and Periphas for about USD 559.3 million. The loans are guaranteed by certain domestic subsidiaries and secured by substantially all assets of the Company and the guarantors.

In May 2026 the holders of the remaining 300,277 preferred shares converted them into 17,103,116 common shares in a non-cash transaction that included about USD 3.3 million of accrued dividends, and the Series A was eliminated. No further new debt was issued in 2026. In September 2026 the U.S. and Canadian securitization facilities were amended to extend maturity to 2030-01-31, which raised borrowing by about USD 58 million and cost about USD 12.5 million of capitalized fees.
A third amendment to the Credit Agreement is dated 2026-06-30 and appears in the exhibit index; its terms are not described in the filings supplied.

## Findings
### Bottom line

OPENLANE's fundamental credit is solid for a high yield issuer: the corporate term loan is lightly levered and well covered by liquidity, but the finance arm's securitization funding and large buybacks mean group-level gearing and cash leakage are higher than the headline.

Total debt is 1.18x twelve-month EBITDA and 1.40x adjusted EBITDA, liquidity is USD 650.2 million, and no corporate debt matures before 2028 apart from scheduled term loan amortization. Net debt is USD 289.3 million, or 0.64x, and USD 300.4 million, or 0.67x, pro forma for USD 11.1 million of repurchases in October 2026. Including USD 2,064.1 million of securitization, total debt is 5.75x EBITDA.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1.1; calculation C1.3; calculation C1.5; calculation C1.7; calculation C2.1
### Key findings

The corporate balance sheet is the strongest support. Total debt is 1.18x twelve-month EBITDA, liquidity is USD 650.2 million, and the term loan amortizes only USD 5.5 million a year to 2032, so debt service does not depend on refinancing in the near term.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C1.1; calculation C1.5

Structural gearing is the main constraint. Securitization funding of USD 2,064.1 million supports finance receivables of USD 2,763.8 million, and with it total debt is 5.75x EBITDA. The facilities recycle and were extended to January 2030, but they are only as good as dealer credit and the bank purchasers' continued commitment.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C1.7

Earnings are rising across two segments. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 382.7 million over twelve months against USD 332.6 million in 2025, of which the marketplace contributed USD 197.7 million and the finance arm USD 185.0 million, and management raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to USD 390 million to USD 400 million.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.3_2026-11-04_q32026openlaneearningssl.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C1.3; calculation C2.2

Cash conversion is good but flattered by settlement timing. Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 309.5 million includes a USD 155.8 million rise in payables, largely offset by a USD 117.0 million rise in receivables, so working capital added USD 38.8 million. After capital expenditure of USD 40.7 million, loan book growth net of its securitization funding, and buybacks of USD 91.5 million, cash generation was USD 132.6 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C3.1; calculation C3.2; calculation C3.3; calculation C3.4

Financial policy is the swing factor. The 2025 preferred take-out was paid for with USD 550.0 million of secured term loans, the preferred has since converted, and governance risk is rated Medium. Buybacks of USD 91.5 million and a larger authorization show that shareholder returns, not debt reduction, are the first call on spare cash.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

The primary downside path starts with dealer stress. Delinquent receivables are 0.6% of receivables managed against 0.3% a year earlier, so a further rise would lift provisions in a segment that earned USD 117.0 million of operating profit in nine months and could tighten securitization terms, while falling volumes would shrink fee revenue and the settlement float. Liquidity of USD 650.2 million and an undrawn revolver give room to absorb the first quarters of such a shock.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1.5
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a solid view is that the headline leverage depends on a perimeter choice: reported EBITDA adds back securitization interest, adjusted EBITDA deducts it, and including securitization funding lifts total debt to adjusted EBITDA to 6.79x. The issuer's own covenant leverage of 0.9x cannot be reproduced from the statements, so the comfort it implies rests on definitions that are not supplied.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C1.8

The view would improve if delinquency stays near 0.6%, buybacks stay below cash generation after loan growth, and the 2028 revolver maturity is extended before it becomes current. It would weaken if net debt rose on a debt-funded return, if the revolver were drawn at a quarter end, or if the amendment dated 2026-06-30 proved to have loosened restricted payment limits.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40
### Limitations
No ratings, market prices or peer set were supplied, so this view is a fundamental one and carries no relative value or rating conclusion.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)
No forecast model was supplied; the only forward evidence is management's 2026 guidance, which is management's own and was raised at each of the three quarterly releases of 2026.
Basis: EX-99.3_2026-05-05_q12026openlaneearningssl.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.3_2026-08-04_q22026openlaneearningssl.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.3_2026-11-04_q32026openlaneearningssl.htm.jsonl, page 5
Legal capacity, recovery and covenant headroom are outside this synthesis and are not assessed, because the executed agreements were not supplied.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strength one is low corporate leverage with ample liquidity. Corporate total debt is 1.18x twelve-month EBITDA and liquidity is USD 650.2 million, so a downturn would have to be deep before the term loan came under pressure, and the revolver covenant is tested only when it is drawn.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C1.1; calculation C1.5

Strength two is a growing, two-segment earnings base. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 382.7 million over twelve months is above the USD 332.6 million of 2025, with the marketplace and finance arm contributing similar amounts, so a weak quarter in one segment is partly cushioned by the other.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1.3; calculation C2.2

Strength three is a long funding runway. The term loan matures in 2032, the securitization facilities in January 2030 and the revolvers in 2028, so near-term maturities are limited to small term loan instalments and the funding of the loan book is committed.

Strength four is the cleared sponsor overhang. The preferred stock converted to common stock in May 2026 and its cash dividend fell from USD 38.6 million in 2025 to USD 5.3 million in nine months, which reduces the fixed claims ahead of common equity.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

Weakness one is structural gearing. Securitization of USD 2,064.1 million sits outside the corporate debt line, and including it total debt to EBITDA is 5.75x, so creditors of the parent have a residual claim on a finance arm whose loan book is pledged to its own lenders.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1.7

Weakness two is credit exposure to independent dealers. The finance arm lends to about fifteen thousand independent dealers, delinquent receivables have doubled to 0.6% of receivables managed, and loan growth consumed USD 367.6 million of cash in nine months, so a downturn would raise provisions while the loan book still needs funding.

Weakness three is distribution policy. Buybacks of USD 91.5 million in nine months and a larger authorization compete with debt reduction, and the 2025 take-out showed that senior debt can be raised to fund returns to holders.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5

Weakness four is dependence on settlement float and a few seller programs. Accounts payable of USD 827.6 million include consignor proceeds, and commercial volume growth of 46% in the third quarter falls to 17% without the latest commercial customer, so volume and cash flow could both fall if a large program is lost.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; EX-99.3_2026-11-04_q32026openlaneearningssl.htm.jsonl, page 4

## Gaps

No ratings, market prices, peer set or lender presentation were supplied, so the view cannot be placed against peers or the market. Severity Medium; relative value and rating questions remain open. These inputs in the run settings would close it.

The executed credit agreement, the amendment dated 2026-06-30 and the securitization agreements were not supplied, so covenant headroom, restricted payment capacity and priming risk are not tested. Severity High; the synthesis relies on the issuer's own covenant statement. The executed documents would close it.

The unused capacity of the securitization facilities and the split of cash interest between the securitization and the corporate debt are not stated. Severity Medium; liquidity counts only cash and revolvers and cover blends two perimeters. Disclosure of both would close it.
The 2026 guidance is management's and no forecast model was supplied, so the forward view is qualitative. Severity Medium; a forecast would test the downside path in numbers.
